Subject: Re: Redwood integration discovery  recap & next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks for carving out time today   great conversation. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Summary of pain points you called out:
- High latency and unpredictable tail for your current chat/rerank pipeline (esp. during peak batch loads).
- Cost leakage from repeated embedding/rerank calls and duplicated context across requests.
- Need for structured, deterministic outputs for downstream workflows (JSON schema enforcement).
- Security/compliance constraints: VPC + KMS preferred for pilot, logging/audit requirements.

Goals you outlined:
- Replace current hosted embeddings + custom reranker with a single inference-backed rerank flow (embeddings + reranking endpoint) to reduce end-to-end latency and cost.
- Support streaming responses for in-product chat and function-calling for actions (ticket creation, lookup).
- Deliver structured outputs (JSON) to your downstream orchestrator for deterministic parsing.

How Redwood fits (integration & product fit recap):
- SDK changes: you can integrate with our Node/Python SDKs; typical change is swapping in our client and initializing with your API key or private endpoint. We support both sync and streaming gRPC/HTTP paths.
- Function calling: Redwood supports a function-calling pattern (schema + arguments) so your UI can request actions and receive structured function results. Works with streaming (partial function arguments during long responses).
- Streaming & structured outputs: streaming to the client is supported; we can emit delta tokens and also enforce structured output via top-level JSON schemas or our "structured output" mode to reduce post-processing.
- Embeddings & reranking: we can host embedding models and provide an embeddings + rerank flow where embeddings are cached and reranking is offered as a single API call to reduce round trips.
- Deployment options: for pilot we can run on Redwood Hosted with a private project, or Dedicated/Private if you need VPC/KMS and stricter isolation.

Attachments (stubs): architecture_diagram.pdf (high-level flow), redwood_integration_playbook.md (integration checklist), demo_recording_stub.mp4 (meeting recording).

Proposed next steps:
1) Tech deep dive (30-45m) with Rishi to walk implementation details, sample SDK snippets, and latency/cost expectations — please share 2x preferred slots next week.
2) Security contacts: Tom, please confirm who owns security/compliance and we'll loop in our Security Solutions Engineer for the SSO/KMS questionnaire.
3) Pilot scope: agree on a small rerank+chat path for an initial 6-week pilot (traffic and success metrics: p95 latency target, cost per 1k queries, accuracy on your eval set).
4) We'll follow up with a model/quantization recommendation and a tailored latency/cost sheet.

If that looks right I can send a calendar invite and a one-page pilot proposal.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Couple of quick clarifications/questions: 
- Our primary pilot will be the help-center reranker + chat integration. We need the rerank call to be <250ms p50 ideally. If that's not achievable on hosted, we can evaluate Dedicated.
- On structured outputs: we rely heavily on consistent JSON to avoid a downstream parsing layer. Do you have examples of schema enforcement or a validation step?
- Security: I'll introduce you to our security lead, Priya (priya.k@acme.com). She'll need the questionnaire and an architecture diagram for VPC/KMS.
- Can you share a short Node SDK snippet for streaming and a separate example for embeddings+rerank? Also a rough cost estimate for the pilot (ballpark monthly based on projected volume ~200k queries/month).

If you can send the SDK examples + a pilot cost ballpark by Monday, that would help speed approvals.

Thanks Tom — great questions. Quick replies inline and next steps.

- Latency: we'll produce a model-specific latency profile for your traffic shape. For many customers the hosted path meets p50 targets for light to moderate token sizes; Dedicated gives more predictable tails. We'll include p50/p95 estimates per model and guidance on batching/kv-cache to meet the <250ms p50 target for rerank flows.

- Structured output enforcement: we have a "structured output" mode that validates against a provided JSON schema and returns either a validated payload or a controlled failure (with validation errors). I'll attach a short technical_brief.pdf with examples.

- SDK snippets: attached below are two short examples (Node streaming + Python embeddings+rerank) — I'll also paste the Node streaming snippet into the follow-up doc for quick copy/paste.

- Security: thanks for looping Priya. Rishi will run through our security checklist and the SSO/KMS options in the tech deep dive.
